# College-Student B2C App Ideas: A Defensible No-Go

*Run: run-20260603-215608 · 4 rounds · 18 hypotheses · 18 rejections · 27/120 LLM-call budget (stopped at evidence saturation) · Perplexity-grounded · June 2026*

## Executive summary

Across four rounds, this run generated eighteen distinct AI-core, student-pays B2C app concepts ($5-15/mo) under a novelty-primary screen — and killed all eighteen, each with a named, specific killer (a shipping competitor, a regulatory wall, a structural adoption failure, or a feasibility ceiling). No two ideas ever survived simultaneously, so the Elo tournament never ran; it didn't need to. The signal was not "we couldn't find the best idea" but "there is no idea here that clears the bar." The run stopped at 27 of 120 budget because the doctrine map reached evidence saturation: every structurally distinct strategy had been probed and had failed for a reason that *generalizes*.

This is a rare and valuable outcome. A no-go that is merely "we didn't find anything" wastes a founder's time. A no-go that explains *why the entire region is empty* — and tells you exactly which constraint to relax to reopen it — is as actionable as a winner. The taxonomy below is the deliverable.

## The verdict and why it's trustworthy

The credibility of a no-go rests on whether the search was structurally diverse or just shallow repetition of one bad idea. This search deliberately attacked the space from four orthogonal strategic angles, and each angle died for a *different* reason — which is what makes the conclusion a thesis rather than an accident.

- **Round 1 — "better tools for existing study tasks" (5/5 killed).** The obvious quadrant. Every idea (authorship provenance, lab copilot, answer-withholding math checker, paid peer Q&A, voice-graded audio flashcards) was already shipping under a named competitor at a comparable price, or was blocked by an integrity-category ban, or had a feasibility flaw (VLM OCR silently *fixes* the student errors it's supposed to catch, 42-66% of the time).
- **Round 2 — "system-shaped ideas with moats" (5/5 killed).** Deliberately harder targets with network or data structure. Killed by competitor swarms (the oral-rehearsal idea faced JurisNote, BarristerAI, VivaCoach *and* ChatGPT Voice), by game theory (free-riders will not opt into a contribution-tracking ledger), by the fact that the measured activity degrades under measurement (evaluation pressure impairs studying; instrumental networking reads as "dirty"), and by frequency math (office hours happen 2-6 times a semester — not a subscription).
- **Round 3 — "non-academic life + new segments" (3/4 killed, 1 survivor).** Moved off campus academics entirely. F-1 status engine hit the UPL wall (unauthorized practice of immigration law is criminally enforced). Shift replanner hit availability-inversion (you set the template once and the daily decisions evaporate) *and* the fact that every shift API is employer-admin-gated. Health navigator hit FDA CDS territory. One idea limped out alive: the Runway financial-aid cashflow engine.
- **Round 4 — "harden the survivor + final probes" (4/4 killed, then the survivor killed).** Four fresh probes died (CBORD platform-risk, free incumbent CampusESP, GET/Penn-Mobile already shipping the fusion, Canvas OAuth requiring institutional keys). Then the final red-team killed Runway itself: TouchNet, Nelnet, BankMobile, CampusESP, and iGrad all deliver every cliff warning and refund alert *free and natively*, leaving a residual that is a one-time calculator with no load-bearing AI.

Eighteen kills, four independent failure mechanisms, zero survivors. That structural diversity is why the no-go is trustworthy.
